scope: read-only UUID identity probe on disposable Ubuntu/ext4 loop storage

checks.findmnt_and_link_agree: passed through the real unprivileged LinuxExt4VolumeProbe after normal udev settle
checks.link_only: passed after the findmnt UUID command was stubbed to return empty; the mountinfo, source-device, /dev directory, and udev-link checks remained real
checks.conflict: rejected as volume_uuid_source_conflict when findmnt was stubbed to return a different canonical UUID
checks.duplicate_matching_links: rejected as ambiguous_volume_uuid_link after temporarily adding a second canonical UUID link to the same block device
checks.malformed_matching_link: rejected as invalid_volume_uuid_link after temporarily adding a malformed link to the mounted block device
checks.wrong_device_link: ignored a temporary canonical UUID link targeting /dev/loop0; the correct /dev/loop1 link remained the unique match
checks.unsafe_directory: unit-tested for non-directory, non-root owner, and group/world-writable modes; no live /dev permission change was made
checks.fresh_clone_setup: passed make setup in a new private read-only GitHub clone at the exact source commit

independent_distribution_builds.result: identical across two independent source clones at the exact commit

limitations: The link-only path was exercised on a synthetic loop image, not a provider-attached research volume.
The conflict case injects only the findmnt output; the udev UUID link and mounted device are real.
This does not qualify broad storage-writer behavior, crash durability, or real Brain data.
